_README: Expected ASSEMBLED-GADGET ground truth per OTG mouse mode.
Keys are '<mode>/hw=<true|false>' because horizontal_wheel changes both
report_length and the descriptor bytes: the same logical mode has a
different correct answer on a rig with the wheel on than off. The test
appliance (10.10.132.110) runs hw=true; pikvm01 runs hw=false. A spec that
ignored this would go red on a perfectly correct box.
An entry carrying a 'placeholder' field returns NOT-VERIFIED (exit 2), not
PASS. Modes are gated only once someone records what they should actually
look like. Green-because-nothing-was-compared is the failure mode this
table is shaped to prevent.
'protocol'/'subclass' are USB HID interface fields, NOT descriptor content:
a change to them is invisible in the descriptor bytes. Both are asserted
separately for that reason.
DO NOT DELETE THE protocol/subclass ASSERTIONS. There is a standing (and
correct) team warning that reads 'NEVER use proto/subclass' — it means
never use them as a STANDALONE MODE ORACLE, because the stock relative
maker already reads 2/1, so '2/1 therefore iPad' is a false positive. That
is a different claim from what this table does. Here they are per-named-
function, per-mode expectations: hid.usb1 must read 0/0 in desktop (it is
the absolute maker there) and 2/1 in ipad (the relative maker there). The
same slot changes maker between modes, which is exactly what makes the
fields informative. A descriptor hash cannot substitute: an absolute/
relative mix-up in the interface fields leaves the report descriptor
untouched, and that blind spot is what made a byte-compare the wrong tool
for the #51 dead-code question.
Descriptor sha256 is over the bytes configfs actually returns for
report_desc (which reads short of its page-sized st_size).
PINNED TO kvmd 4.188 (python3.14). The descriptor is a pure function of
(absolute, horizontal_wheel) FOR A GIVEN kvmd VERSION, so these values are
rig-independent but NOT version-independent. If kvmd is bumped, re-derive
before trusting them.
ALL FOUR WERE COMPUTED LOCALLY on the appliance's own kvmd 4.188, by
importing the module the running unit actually resolves and calling
make_mouse_hid() across the four (absolute, horizontal_wheel) combinations.
NONE was transcribed from another rig. Re-derived 2026-08-07 and all four
reproduced identically.
Independent confirmation differs PER ARM, and the difference matters when
diagnosing a surprise:
abs/hw1 3a71a5a2 - computed AND matches this appliance's live configfs
(hid.usb1). Two sources.
rel/hw1 92155ddf - computed AND matches this appliance's live configfs
(hid.usb2). Two sources.
rel/hw0 55c045b2 - computed here AND matches pikvm01's live gadget, a
DIFFERENT kvmd tree (4.121, python3.13). Two sources
across two versions, so this arm is the best-evidenced
of the four and demonstrates the generator is stable
across 4.121<->4.188 for this combination.
abs/hw0 d9b93f5a - computed ONLY, and the ONLY arm with no measurement
anywhere. No rig in the fleet assembles an absolute
mouse with the wheel off, so nothing can currently
falsify it. Do NOT let it inherit the credibility of
the three arms above: this table is not uniformly
hardware-confirmed, and a green does not mean all four
were checked against silicon. (Raised by the iPad node,
pikvm-mcp-server@georgs-mac-mini — correctly.)
It is kept rather than deleted because it IS reachable,
just not by either #51 mode's defaults: `desktop` pins
mouse.absolute=true and mouse_alt.device but leaves
horizontal_wheel UNPINNED, so desktop + a user-set
hid.mouse.horizontal_wheel=false lands the primary mouse
exactly here (with rel/hw0 as the alt). If that config
ever appears, this pin meets real hardware for the first
time — treat a mismatch there as un-cross-checked rather
than as a regression, and take the opportunity to source
it properly.
`ipad` pins horizontal_wheel=false explicitly, so the
iPad path never reaches this arm.
A surprise on rel/hw0 should be read as 'the measurement is wrong', not
'the value is version-dependent' — byte-level evidence with a positive
control already says it is not.

_selftest-placeholder/hw=true.placeholder: PERMANENT TEST FIXTURE — not a real mode, never selected by anything. It exists so the NOT-VERIFIED path stays exercised forever. Once every real mode has expectations, the 'unspecced mode must not report green' guarantee would otherwise become untested, and an untested guarantee is one regression away from being false. Do not delete; do not fill in.

_provenance: MEASURED on the appliance 2026-08-07, generation
51fzka7saj8hmagqqvmw8a138fcg0kng (main f6d8d70), kvmd 4.188, aarch64,
services.pikvm.kvmd.ipadCompat DISABLED.
The three descriptor hashes were independently reproduced by running
kvmd's own make_mouse_hid() under the interpreter the unit actually
uses, and matched the live configfs bytes exactly — so this table is
anchored to the kernel's view, not to a reading of the source.

functions.name: hid.usb1
functions._what: primary mouse — ABSOLUTE, horizontal_wheel=true. protocol=0/subclass=0 is stock-unpatched; ipadCompat's postPatch would move these to 2/1, so this pair is what distinguishes patched from unpatched at runtime.

functions.name: hid.usb2
functions._what: alt mouse — RELATIVE, horizontal_wheel=true. protocol=2/subclass=1 is UPSTREAM STOCK for the relative maker, not evidence of any patch.

_provenance: Specced by pikvm-nixos@nixos-developer-system 2026-08-07: 'desktop'
is the stock shape — absolute primary mouse + relative alt, wheel on.
Byte-for-byte the same expectation as stock-default/hw=true above,
which was MEASURED on the appliance. Kept as a separate entry rather
than an alias so that if the two ever diverge the table says so out
loud instead of silently following one of them.

functions.name: hid.usb2
functions._what: alt mouse — relative (kvmd gives the alt the INVERSE of mouse.absolute), wheel on

_provenance: Specced by pikvm-nixos@nixos-developer-system 2026-08-07 and VERIFIED
against kvmd 4.188 source on the appliance before being recorded:
apps/otg/__init__.py __add_hid names functions 'hid.usb{instance}'
from a sequential counter, so keyboard=usb0 and the primary mouse
=usb1; the alt mouse is added ONLY under
`if config.kvmd.hid.mouse_alt.device:`, so device="" means no usb2.
The primary mouse takes mouse.absolute directly (false here =>
relative); the alt would take its inverse.
The keyboard hash is reused from the measured baseline, and that reuse
is sound rather than assumed: make_keyboard_hid() takes no arguments,
so no mouse setting can reach it.

functions.name: hid.usb1
functions._what: the ONLY mouse — relative, wheel OFF. protocol=2/subclass=1 is stock for the relative maker, NOT evidence of a patch.

_provenance: CONTINGENT variant, recorded so the table can answer either way the
open design question lands. nixos-developer-system's design forces
horizontal_wheel=false in iPad mode, which makes ipad/hw=false the
active entry; that choice is NOT yet confirmed by manager/georg. If
they flip it to leave the wheel on, this becomes the active entry.
Same single-relative-mouse shape, wheel-on descriptor: report_length
5 and the hash measured for the relative hw=true maker.
Holding both costs nothing and removes a scramble later; the mode
selection decides which one is asserted, so a wrong guess here can
never silently gate the wrong shape.

functions.name: hid.usb1
functions._what: the ONLY mouse — relative, wheel ON
